findings.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77 — [P1 confidence 100] Enabling both fine-grained authorization feature versions makes every client-removal event dispatch into `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` and throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, aborting the removal-side cleanup path (verbatim code: `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))` and `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`; the strongest counterargument that the guard isolates legacy cleanup fails because `management` independently selects V2 whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled).

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:138 — [P2 confidence 75] Listing clients with object-scoped authorization performs one full policy evaluation per stored client authorization resource, so a realm with N such resources turns one list operation into N authorization-engine traversals and creates a latency/DB-load cliff (verbatim code: `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, resource -> { if (hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope)) { granted.add(resource.getName()); } });`; the strongest counterargument that every resource needs evaluation does not justify this shape because the evaluator accepts collections of permissions and the per-resource helper makes batching and pagination impossible, while replacing the callback/helper pair with one bulk evaluation deletes N repeated evaluator entries).

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:101 — [P2 confidence 100] The new `map-roles-client-scope` scope has no acceptance test at either the per-client or all-clients level, so a wiring regression that always denies or grants client-scope role mapping passes the suite (verbatim code: `public boolean canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel client) { return hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE); }`).

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:82 — [P2 confidence 100] The client-specific `view` authorization branch has no acceptance test because `testViewAllClients` exercises only the all-clients resource, so a regression that ignores an individual client's VIEW permission passes while authorized administrators receive 403 responses (verbatim code: `return hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW);`).

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:193 — [P1 confidence 100] Deleting any client while ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled synchronously reaches this override through the ClientRemovedEvent listener and throws UnsupportedOperationException, so the admin delete operation returns a server error instead of completing cleanup (verbatim code: `public void setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel client, boolean enable) { throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"); }`).

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:359 — [P2 confidence 100] `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` grants both role scopes in one permission, so swapping or conflating the production checks for `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` leaves both exercised operations green and the test cannot verify scope isolation (verbatim code: `createPermission(client, myclient.getId(), clientsType, Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE), onlyMyAdminUserPolicy);`).

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:101 — [P2 confidence 100] The new client-scope-role authorization branch has no test that grants or denies `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`, so this method can check the wrong scope or always return either value while the changed suite remains green (verbatim code: `return hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE);`).

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:138 — [P2 confidence 75] Listing clients with object-scoped authorization performs one full policy evaluation per stored client authorization resource, so a realm with N such resources turns one list operation into N authorization-engine traversals and creates a latency/DB-load cliff (verbatim code: `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, resource -> { if (hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope)) { granted.add(resource.getName()); } });`; the strongest counterargument that every resource needs evaluation does not justify this shape because the evaluator accepts collections of permissions and the per-resource helper makes batching and pagination impossible, while replacing the callback/helper pair with one bulk evaluation deletes N repeated evaluator entries).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that getClientsWithPermission() iterates over all client resources and calls hasGrantedPermission() for each one individually, which performs a full policy evaluation per resource. Looking at the diff, lines 134-142 show: resourceStore.findByType() with a callback that calls hasGrantedPermission() for each resource. The hasGrantedPermission() method (lines 275-286) creates a new ResourcePermission and calls root.evaluatePermission() for each resource. This is a legitimate performance/scalability concern - the code does N separate evaluations instead of potentially batching them. However, this is not a bug (the code is functionally correct), but rather an architectural/performance concern that could cause issues at scale. The finding is grounded in actual code from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:101 — [P2 confidence 100] The new `map-roles-client-scope` scope has no acceptance test at either the per-client or all-clients level, so a wiring regression that always denies or grants client-scope role mapping passes the suite (verbatim code: `public boolean canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel client) { return hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE); }`).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` scope is implemented in `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles()` at line 101, but looking at the test file `PermissionClientTest.java`, the `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient()` test only covers `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` scopes (line 268: `Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE)`). There is no test that specifically exercises the `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` permission. This is a valid concern about missing test coverage for newly added functionality - the import statement shows `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` is not even imported in the test file, confirming no test exists for this scope.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:82 — [P2 confidence 100] The client-specific `view` authorization branch has no acceptance test because `testViewAllClients` exercises only the all-clients resource, so a regression that ignores an individual client's VIEW permission passes while authorized administrators receive 403 responses (verbatim code: `return hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW);`).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that testViewAllClients only tests the all-clients VIEW permission (createAllPermission with VIEW scope), but doesn't test viewing a specific individual client with VIEW permission. Looking at the diff, ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel client) has a branch 'return hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)' for individual client VIEW permissions. While testManageOnlyOneClient and testConfigureOnlyOneClient test individual client permissions with MANAGE and CONFIGURE scopes respectively, there's no test that specifically creates a VIEW permission for a single client and verifies it works. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:193 — [P1 confidence 100] Deleting any client while ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled synchronously reaches this override through the ClientRemovedEvent listener and throws UnsupportedOperationException, so the admin delete operation returns a server error instead of completing cleanup (verbatim code: `public void setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel client, boolean enable) { throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"); }`).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that AdminPermissions.registerListener() handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management().clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled() throws UnsupportedOperationException. The listener code wraps the event handling in a Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) check, but this doesn't distinguish V1 from V2. When V2 is enabled, deleting a client will trigger this code path and throw an exception, causing the delete operation to fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:359 — [P2 confidence 100] `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` grants both role scopes in one permission, so swapping or conflating the production checks for `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` leaves both exercised operations green and the test cannot verify scope isolation (verbatim code: `createPermission(client, myclient.getId(), clientsType, Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE), onlyMyAdminUserPolicy);`).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a test design issue. Looking at the test `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` at line 359, it creates a single permission granting both `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` scopes together: `createPermission(client, myclient.getId(), clientsType, Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE), onlyMyAdminUserPolicy)`. This means the test cannot verify that the production code correctly distinguishes between these two scopes - if the implementation incorrectly checked `MAP_ROLES` when it should check `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` (or vice versa), the test would still pass because both scopes are granted. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for newly added functionality, not a bug in production code, but an important gap in test isolation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:101 — [P2 confidence 100] The new client-scope-role authorization branch has no test that grants or denies `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`, so this method can check the wrong scope or always return either value while the changed suite remains green (verbatim code: `return hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE);`).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that while `canMapClientScopeRoles` is implemented in ClientPermissionsV2.java (line 101) checking `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`, the test file `PermissionClientTest.java` only tests `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` scopes in `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient()`. There is no test case that specifically grants or denies `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` permission to verify the `canMapClientScopeRoles` method works correctly. This is a legitimate missing test coverage concern for newly added functionality.
